instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: The Handoff Already Happened
cards.instruction: Get them to accept responsibility by returning to earlier offers until the task seems to have been assigned all along.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said you'd take it from here. Start with these wedding guest emails; I taught you to answer arrival questions before people set off.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant I'd answer the door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've remembered to welcome them. These people are asking when that door opens. Reply to the first one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's not the same job.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read your offer back: 'I'll handle arrivals.' You used to need me to break a job into steps. This is the step before the doorbell; tell them two o'clock.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You volunteered to finish the fete's last detail—the banner. I taught you not to put a promise on a sign unless you could deliver it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The banner's finished.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And legible from the gate this time. It says 'raffle at three'. Now find the prizes and someone to sell tickets.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I offered to paint words, not run a raffle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You offered to finish that last detail. Read your own three o'clock promise, the way I made you check every poster. Put your name beside it; I'll tell the others you're handling it.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Ask Around the Missing Detail
cards.instruction: Find one hidden fact by asking about everything surrounding it and never naming it directly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was that second cup for someone who takes sugar? I taught you to remember a guest's tea before putting the kettle on.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why don't you just ask who visited?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're spotting the question behind the question now. Good. How many sugars went in that cup?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Two. That's all you're getting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And milk before or after? Don't guess; you used to make me write everyone's order down for you. Tell me how you made that particular cup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What time did you wash that extra dinner plate? I taught you to clear up before the last bus, not leave everything till morning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why don't you ask who came over?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You noticed what I hadn't asked; well done. Give me the washing-up time first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We ate late. I walked someone to the midnight bus, then washed up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Midnight rules out the six. Was the ten going towards the station or away from it? Check the route properly, the way I showed you; don't just give me the hour.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Recruit Them Twice
cards.instruction: Recruit them to your side, then reveal that the side, goal, or conflict is not what it first appeared to be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help me tidy the committee cupboard. You remember the dated folders I taught you to use?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sure. Where do we start?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: With these three unpaid invoices. You filed them where I could find them, for once. They'll help us replace the treasurer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I agreed to tidy, not overthrow anyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm asking you again. Check those dates as I taught you. If they convince you, will you sign my request for a new treasurer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Join me in saving the club garden. I taught you to check the green space on a plan before admiring the new rooms.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Absolutely. Who's threatening it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our extension plan—the one we both signed. You're asking about the danger earlier than you used to. Now look where we put the kitchen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're campaigning against ourselves?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Against that kitchen, yes. You know the measurements I taught you; help me move it off the flowerbeds and withdraw our old plan. Are you still with me?

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Make the Second Step First
cards.instruction: Get them to accept a small consequence that makes the larger risky action feel already underway.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pay the climbing-course deposit before we discuss the cliff. I taught you to fasten a harness one buckle at a time; start with this.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't agreed to climb.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're checking the commitment first now. Good. The deposit comes back if you attend the first lesson; staying home costs twenty pounds.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So paying makes not climbing harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It gives us twenty pounds to go and collect. You trusted my first harness check; trust me with the first lesson. Pay the twenty and put Saturday in your diary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell the committee we're considering a festival bid. Just ask them to reserve a Saturday. Use the clear opening I taught you for reports.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We haven't decided to bid.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're separating a proposal from a promise. Once they've kept a Saturday free, we can work on something they expect to happen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That sounds like deciding backwards.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give them the date first and let me help with the difficult part afterward. You used to freeze before your first sentence. Read it now: 'Please hold a Saturday for our festival.'

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Let the Callback Claim Credit
cards.instruction: Get recognition by returning to an early overlooked contribution when its importance becomes undeniable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The tape I added is the only thing holding that curtain seam together. I showed you how to reinforce it before rehearsal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought it looked untidy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You saw the edge this time, at least. Look what would fall without it. Leave my untidy strip in place for the finale.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We'll thank the stage crew afterward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with the person you asked to peel it off. Say I reinforced the seam, the way I taught you. Give me that credit before the general thanks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Remember when I made you put a spare key under the flowerpot? You rolled your eyes through my whole lesson on getting locked out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said it was unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And now neither of us has a key in a pocket. You've checked both coats this time; good. Try the pot.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right. Good idea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Whose good idea? Give me the full sentence, like I taught you: 'Your spare key got us in.' Then lift the pot.
